Build the Wide Model Dataset for a Chosen Panel

Source: R/profile_eligibility.R
profile_prepare_model_data.Rd

Stage 3 of the resistance-profiling pipeline: turns long- or wide-format AST data, restricted to one chosen panel of antibiotic classes, into the Y matrix profile_build_design expects (events x classes, entries in c(0, 1, NA)), plus everything needed to trace and model it: group/event identifiers, a covariate table, and an exclusion manifest for events with nothing in the panel tested at all.

Usage

profile_prepare_model_data(
  data,
  group_col,
  panel,
  class_col = NULL,
  value_col = "antibiotic_value",
  resistant_values = c("R", "Resistant", "resistant"),
  susceptible_values = c("S", "Susceptible", "susceptible"),
  intermediate_values = c("I", "Intermediate", "intermediate"),
  intermediate_as_resistant = TRUE,
  event_id_col = NULL,
  covariates = NULL,
  unknown_action = c("error", "treat_as_untested"),
  conflict_action = c("error", "drop_conflicts", "resistant_wins", "susceptible_wins",
    "first"),
  covariate_conflict_action = c("error", "first")
)

Arguments

data, group_col, class_col, value_col, resistant_values, susceptible_values, intermediate_values, event_id_col

Same as profile_audit_support. event_id_col is required (not optional) for long-format data – a real per-event key is needed to merge covariates back onto the wide outcome matrix.

panel

Character vector. The chosen panel's classes – becomes colnames(Y), in this order.

intermediate_as_resistant

Logical. Same meaning as in profile_audit_support; controls whether Y folds "I" into 1 (resistant) or leaves it untested (NA).

covariates

Character vector of column names in data to carry into the returned covariate table, one value per event. Rows sharing an event_id_col value are checked for agreement on every requested covariate first; see covariate_conflict_action. Default NULL (no covariates carried – just Y and identifiers).

unknown_action, conflict_action

Same meaning as in profile_audit_support – the shared AST policy for susceptibility RESULTS, applied identically here.

covariate_conflict_action

Character, "error" (default) or "first". A DIFFERENT conflict from conflict_action above: this one is about COVARIATE values (e.g. age, ward) disagreeing across the several raw rows that share one event_id_col value, not about AST results. "error" stops, naming every event id and covariate where rows disagree – silently keeping whichever row happened to come first is exactly the failure mode this guards against. "first" restores the old behavior (take the first row's value) for callers who have already verified, outside this function, that their covariates are event-invariant.

Value

A list:

Y

matrix, events x length(panel), entries in c(0, 1, NA), column names = panel

ids

data frame, one row per event matching Y's rows: event_id, group

covariates

data frame, one row per event matching Y's rows, the requested covariates columns (zero columns if none requested)

status

character vector, one per event: "complete" (every panel class tested) or "partial"

manifest

one-row data frame: n_events_input, n_events_excluded_untested (no panel class tested at all), n_events_output (= nrow(Y)), n_complete, n_partial

Details

Covariates are returned as a plain table, not a model-matrix design – identifiers (patient id, hospital, admission id) are carried for grouping and provenance only and do not automatically become predictors or random effects. Build the actual X passed to profile_build_design from this table with model.matrix() and whatever formula the model specification calls for; that choice belongs to the caller (the analysis repository's model config), not to this function.

Every event counted as model-eligible here is the set that profile_audit_support/profile_check_panel_feasibility should be RE-RUN against once this function has dropped events with nothing tested in the panel at all (or, if a covariate's completeness is later enforced downstream, re-run again on whatever survives that too) – support computed only on the pre-cohort-selection or pre-covariate- reconciliation data describes a bigger cohort than the one that actually reaches the model.
